video_title: Analytics in the NBA (with Dean Oliver), Knick's Extension Talks, and Space Jam Jordans

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Podziemski's 5-year $110M contract extension with the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: Brandon “Air Podz” Podziemski signs a 5 year $110M extension with the Warriors
quotes.quote: Brandon “Air Podz” Podziemski signs a 5 year $110M extension with the Warriors. They call him Air Podz, that's hard. He's 23 years old now and last year averaged 14 points, 5 rebounds and 4 assists and 37% from 3, which I honestly think he's another one of those guys that if we're talking to analytics, he's another one of those guys that has to shoot a couple more than he really wants to, but that's because of the role and system that he's in. He's actually a better 3-point shooter than he gets a lot of credit for.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Should the Spurs start Dylan Harper on opening night?
quotes.excerpt: Should the Spurs starting lineup include Dylan Harper on opening night? Yes, the fucking should.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: Should the Spurs starting lineup include Dylan Harper on opening night? Yes, the fucking should. The only reason it shouldn't is if you feel like your bench just ain't got it. If you feel like your bench ain't got what it takes, then start the man, take him out in first rotation and let him come back in for second rotation. But he needs to play the first four minutes of the game.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: I agree this is something y'all can play around with and tease the idea of him doing that for the rest of the season, but he's coming off that bench. This was needed for Champagnie being out, but you want him off the bench. His defense, his ability to get to the basket and this year I feel like he's going to get more attempts at the free throw line, he's going to be a little bit more efficient, you want him coming off the bench.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' decision to delay contract extensions for Towns and Hart
quotes.excerpt: I don't like this at all. They should be ashamed of themselves.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: I don't like this at all. They should be ashamed of themselves. Y'all getting the second apron, it's okay. It's okay. Y'all finna get, yeah, y'all getting second aprons. It's going to be about five, six aprons on y'all.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: That's understandable if you're Josh Hart, really, but if I'm Karl-Anthony Towns, I feel different.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart's response to Knicks contract extension delay
quotes.excerpt: At the end of the day, I'm still under contract in New York.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: He had all the reason to bash y'all, throw you under the bus. He just love basketball, got a great life. He not worried about it. So let me worry about it for you Josh. Pay that man, dog. Pay that man. What we doing? James Dolan, you got great guys on your team, pay these men, Joe.

text_blocks.speaker: Arhii Shumpert
text_blocks.text: It was news to me. Very disappointed to say the least. Let's state the obvious, it's business, but there is business on the court for us to handle.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Oliver on the role of analytics in modern NBA coaching
quotes.excerpt: I want the numbers to give me some insight about how I'm going to make you a better player.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: Do you feel like there is parts of using analytics that shouldn't be used?

text_blocks.speaker: Dean Oliver
text_blocks.text: I think people distort things. I think people will exaggerate things to make a point. Like you say, it's show business. Sometimes show business is exaggerating things to make a point. I think when you're doing media, that's one thing. You can exaggerate to make a point and I think that's a lot of what we hear. But when you're on a team, when I'm coaching you, I don't want to lie to you. I want the numbers to give me some insight about how I'm going to make you a better player. And hopefully you're getting that from tape, hopefully we're getting that from other people's independent perspectives too. But we're just trying to put it together for the team to make the players better, not only who you are as an individual, but how you play with your teammates.

quotes.speaker: Dean Oliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Oliver on using analytics to evaluate clutch play
quotes.excerpt: It needs to be a conversation. I think that is the most important thing.
quotes.quote: It needs to be a conversation. I think that is the most important thing. Why is this different from what I see with my eyes? And I'll give you a couple reasons why it might be. One is clutch play. Jalen Brunson, we all on the Knicks can play in the clutch. But he like, we also know that he's not the greatest defender. He's a smaller guy. We also know that like, okay, there's not a lot of clutch plays in a lot of games. Like a lot of games come down to like, okay, they're up by 17 and with five minutes to go. Like you're not going to get all that. And he may take some plays off because he can. So if we're looking at clutch play, yeah, Jalen Brunson has been great for sure, but that's not the only criteria. Sometimes you want to be Mr. First Quarter. And first quarter, like I can tell you most of the best players in the NBA, you're either Jokic, you're Doncic, you're Giannis, you're SGA. That start off hitting you in the mouth.

quotes.speaker: Dean Oliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Oliver on evaluating player performance beyond box score stats
quotes.excerpt: When the narratives have already been generated and the numbers don't necessarily support it, you have to swim upstream.
quotes.quote: I think a lot of times the narrative has already been built. And I think when the narratives have already been generated and the numbers don't necessarily support it, you have to swim upstream. Once that happens, it's tough. And sometimes like who is the MVP gets decided fairly or like Asia Wilson last year, not this year so much. Asia Wilson wasn't playing great in the WNBA in the first half of the season. She was still good, but she's always good. She picked it up late. And so how much should the second half of the season count versus the first half of the season? And like okay, the narrative started getting built when they went on like a 12 game winning streak or something like that. And like okay, should she be MVP when the piece of Asia Wilson was having a great season herself? That kind of stuff.
